    Read a whole board

    Drag a screenshot here from Finder, paste with ⌘V, or pick a file. Mesa reads every player's table and makes one tab per video pane.

    Your hand is replaced by whatever is found. To just add cards, close this view and paste among the cards instead.

    Suggestions
      Screenshots
      Click a marker to change that card · click empty space to add one · ⌘V swaps the image and re-reads the whole board

      Paste card names

      One card name per line. A count in front works (2 Sol Ring, 1x Llanowar Elves), as does a set suffix from decklists (Sol Ring (LTC) 268). Typos are corrected automatically where possible.

      Camera

      Phone connected
      How the camera works

      Scan the code with your phone's camera — nothing to install. You sign in with the same account, and the phone becomes your camera in this game. Put it in a holder straight above your cards, and keep the deck and the graveyard out of the picture.

      Picture mode · MES-229 · MES-244

      Default: 4K · 15 fps, one frame every 150 ms. The phone retakes its reference picture when the mode changes.

      Recording probe · MES-190

      Connect the phone with ?debug open on it, then start a pass.

      Latency · MES-215

        Connect the phone with ?debug open on it, then start. Every card gets a row per event — shadow, name, tap, move, gone — timed from when your hand lets go of the card until the computer has drawn it.

        Keyboard shortcuts

        Getting around

        Point at a card
        The keys below act on the card under the pointer — there is no selected card
        F Enter
        Focus mode — the card fills the screen; ←→ step through the cards
        Space
        Turn the card over — its other face, or face down
        Space + drag
        Move the mat — or drag with two fingers on the trackpad
        S
        Switch between select and pan. In pan, click and drag anywhere to move the mat
        U
        Untap all — every tapped card on your table stands back up
        Drag on the mat
        In select: mark every card the box touches — ⇧ adds, ⇧-click adds or removes one card. Drag a marked card to move them all; T taps them all; Esc or a click on the mat clears
        Drag a mana stack
        Moves the whole stack — a click still taps just the card you hit. ⌃ Ctrl + drag takes one card out of the stack (⌥ works too), as does ⋯ on the card
        Esc
        Close overlay / leave the search box

        Players

        ↑↓
        In a game: step between your table, everyone and one opponent — or drag the edge between the tables
        1
        In a game: your table big. Outside a game: switch to player
        2…9
        In a game: an opponent's table big, in the order you sit — the number stands next to their name. Outside a game: switch to player
        E
        In a game: everyone at once
        ←→ Tab
        Next opponent (⇧Tab back). Outside a game: next player
        Click a table
        Makes it big — a drag moves it instead
        N
        New player (outside a game)
        R
        Rename yourself

        Building the board

        L
        In a game: pick up your library. Type a name to find a card, Enter puts it on the table
        ⌘S
        In a game: pick up your library with the search field ready
        / A
        Outside a game: the search box
        ⌘V
        Paste an image — whatever is found is added to the board (outside a game)
        B
        Paste a list of names (outside a game)
        I
        Add cards from an image (outside a game)
        ⌘Z
        Undo the last thing you did on your board — a move, a tap, a card to the graveyard
        T
        Tap or untap the card under the pointer
        E
        Put the card under the pointer on another one — equip, fortify, attach
        G
        Put the card under the pointer in the graveyard. With no card under the pointer: pick up the graveyard
        H
        Return the card under the pointer to your hand
        C
        Counters on the card under the pointer
        D
        Duplicate the card under the pointer

        Image & view

        R
        Read the image again (in the image view)
        1–9
        Pick a candidate when confirming a card
        + −
        Zoom in / out on the table
        0
        Show every card on the table, clear of the library and graveyard
        ?
        This pane

        How Mesa reads a screenshot: it first looks for the video panes (black gaps separate them), then for dark card borders against the light table in each pane, and finally matches every hit against the cards in your deck. Only cards that match clearly are added automatically — the rest end up in the confirm row at the top.

        Matching happens against your deck (the Mesa menu, top left → My decks). That is what makes it work: a hundred cards can be told apart visually, all 30,000 MTG cards cannot. Card data and images come from Scryfall. Everything is stored in this browser only.

        AI help with uncertain cards

        Local recognition handles most cards on its own. For the ones it isn't sure about, an image model can decide — it sees the cropped card and the best candidates, and picks one.

        The app is running without a server, so AI help needs your own key from console.anthropic.com. The key is stored in this browser and only sent to Anthropic — but anyone with access to this computer can read it, so use a separate key with a spending limit.
